channel.title: The Grant Desk - Grants, Research & Journalism, US
channel.description: Paid open calls, fellowships and residencies in AI, tech, research, and digital and mixed-media arts, sorted into the right pile. Updated as new calls land on the desk. Filtered to: Grants, Research & Journalism, US.

item.title: Alicia Patterson Fellowship 2027 (Fund for Investigative Journalism)
item.description:
Organisation: Fund for Investigative Journalism (Alicia Patterson Foundation program)

Location: Remote; fellows may live anywhere, but projects must be U.S.-focused for publication in American outlets

Award: $40,000 (12-month fellowship) or $20,000 (6-month fellowship), paid monthly; covers living and reporting costs

Duration: 6 or 12 months, beginning early 2027

Deadline: 01 Oct 2026

Long-running fellowship for in-depth, investigative written reporting on subjects of public interest, now administered by the Fund for Investigative Journalism after the foundation's December 2025 merger. For seasoned reporters with a body of in-depth written work; freelancers are encouraged and staff journalists may apply if they take leave (part-time work is allowed during the fellowship, full-time is not). Twelve-month fellows produce four articles, six-month fellows two. Decisions by end of 2026. Distinct from FIJ's regular reporting grants. No application fee.

Open call details

item.title: Pulitzer Center: U.S. Local News Reporting Grants (Bringing Stories Home)
item.description:
Organisation: Pulitzer Center

Location: United States (US-based stories)

Award: Reporting grants covering project hard costs (typically no salaries or equipment). No application fee.

Duration: Project-based

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Pulitzer Center's 'Bringing Stories Home' initiative supports in-depth local journalism on under-covered issues in communities across the United States. ELIGIBILITY: freelance and staff journalists working on US-based stories. Grants cover the hard costs of reporting. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis via the Pulitzer Center reporting-grants page.

Open call details

item.title: Foundation for Contemporary Arts: Emergency Grants
item.description:
Organisation: Foundation for Contemporary Arts

Location: United States and US territories

Award: $500 to $3,000 (average ~$2,200)

Duration: Per project

Deadline: Rolling / undated

Year-round support for unanticipated opportunities or emergencies tied to a confirmed innovative artistic project. Open to individual visual and performing artists and poets living in the US or US territories with a US tax ID. Apply 8 to 10 weeks before your public presentation date. Designed to cover sudden costs (a venue change, a confirmed exhibition or performance opportunity with a tight runway, etc.).

Open call details

item.title: Fund for Investigative Journalism (FIJ) Grants
item.description:
Organisation: Fund for Investigative Journalism

Location: USA-primary (foreign-based stories require strong U.S. angle)

Award: Up to $10,000 (regular) or $1,000 to $2,500 (seed)

Duration: Story-based

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

Grants for in-depth investigative reporting that exposes corruption, malfeasance or misuse of power across public and private sectors. Covers print, online, broadcast, books, documentaries and podcasts. Surveillance, abuse-of-power and accountability investigations all fit. Letter of Commitment from a news outlet required for full proposals (not for seed). Seed deadline ~10 May 2026; regular deadline 14 September 2026, 23:59 ET. Reviewed three to four times per year. Stories must be published in English with a U.S. media outlet. Ethnic media and journalists of colour particularly encouraged.

Open call details
